text:
sarah: Quick update — ran a sweep for continuous-batcher + scheduler flags on quantized models (q8/q4f16) across H100 and A100 in us-west, eu-central, and asia-southeast :chart_with_upwards_trend:
kevin: awesome. top-line numbers?
bench-bot: run 1794507890 started by sarah
bench-bot: command:
```
./run_bench --model redwood-13b-q8 --gpu H100 --region us-west --batch_window_ms=12 --max_batch_tokens=1536 --scheduler=continuous
```
sarah: Short summary: H100 q8 p95 latency ~78ms @ throughput 440 seq/s (batch_window 12ms, max_tokens 1536). A100 q8 p95 ~120ms @ 300 seq/s same config. bf16 runs were lower latency but cost ~1.5x.
anika: interesting — how did fairness look for small requests? any tail regressions for single-token prompts?
miguel: saw tail increase on asia-southeast for q8 + larger max_batch_tokens. p99 jumped from 240ms -> 380ms for tiny requests when region throughput peaked.
sarah: yeah, that was our biggest flag. hypothesis: large max_batch_tokens allows oversized batches on high-concurrency hosts which hurts single-user latency.
kevin: did you try reducing batch_window and keeping max_batch_tokens to stop giant batches?
sarah: tried 2 quick configs:
```
# config A (lower window)
batch_window_ms=6
max_batch_tokens=1536
# config B (cap tokens)
batch_window_ms=12
max_batch_tokens=768
```
bench-bot: results (us-west, H100, q8):
- config A: p95=86ms, throughput=410 seq/s, p99=210ms
- config B: p95=92ms, throughput=385 seq/s, p99=160ms
anika: config B seems better for fairness (p99 down). throughput hit is small. prefer capping tokens for interactive apps.
miguel: region note — in eu-central we saw A100 config B p95=135ms, p99=270ms. still heavier than H100 but more stable tails.
kevin: kernel choices? did you force fused-kernel vs fallback?
sarah: ran kernel sweep too. fused matmul kernels helped latency on H100 for q4f16; q8 gains smaller. fallback kernels on older drivers increased p99 by ~30-40ms.
anika: any regressions in quality after quant? subtle drop on code-generation for q4f16 noted in eval set (token-level chrF down ~0.6). documented in the run artifacts.
sarah: noted. trade-off summary in the artifact bucket: q8 gives best cost/latency for chat workloads, q4f16 reduces memory but needs eval gating for code tasks.
kevin: actionable items?
miguel: 1) default scheduler: cap max_batch_tokens=768 for interactive routes. 2) keep batch_window at 10-12ms for throughput routes, lower to 6ms for low-latency routes. 3) add kernel-driver compatibility check in deploy pipeline.
anika: add an eval job that runs the code-gen prompts with q4f16 before rolling.
sarah: will open a PR with scheduler flags + benchmark artifacts and add overnight continuous runs in asia-southeast to validate tails. assigning to @anika for eval job and @miguel for driver checks.
kevin: thanks — please drop the artifacts link when PR is up. :thumbsup:
